grades.quote: FENCE.I does _not_ ensure that other RISC-V harts' instruction fetches will observe the local hart’s stores in a multiprocessor system. To make a store to instruction memory visible to all RISC-V harts, the writing hart also has to execute a data FENCE before requesting that all remote RISC-V harts execute a FENCE.I.
grades.reason: Directly answers: FENCE.I only ensures the local hart's subsequent instruction fetches see its prior stores; it does not ensure other harts' fetches observe them, requiring a data FENCE plus remote FENCE.I.
About SFENCE.VMA and address-translation caches/ASIDs, not FENCE.I instruction-fetch synchronization across harts.
Alloy formal memory model for data FENCE preserved program order; does not address FENCE.I or instruction-fetch synchronization among harts.
Describes SFENCE.VMA, which is a different instruction (memory-management fence) and only locally ordered; it does not discuss FENCE.I. The analogous local-only scope is not about instruction fetch.
